newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.N., aid workers said released in Iran.
newsitem.headline: U.N., aid workers said released in Iran.

text.p: Iran said on Monday it had released a U.N. official, two refugee workers and a driver held in its custody for several days, adding the group had already crossed the border into Iraq, a United Nations official said.
The four were reported to have been seized by an unnamed group in northern Iraq last week and taken into Iran.

"The authorities here (in Iran) tell us that they have been released, that there was no problem, that they went to the border and crossed at 2:45 p.m. (1015 GMT)," United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) official Laurens Jolles said.
"I have no doubt that they have been released," he told Reuters by telephone from Tehran.
Jolles said U.N. officials in Iraq had been waiting for the group at the border. But he said he had not yet received confirmation that the four had arrived.
He said it was not yet clear why the four -- Pierre Vinet, UNHCR representative in northern Iraq, two aid workers with Pharmaciens sans Frontiers and a driver -- were in Iran or how they came there.
PSF said the four were seized near the Iran-Iraq border while visiting refugees displaced in the capture of the Iraqi city of Sulaimaniya.
Sulaimaniya is in the hands of the Iraqi government-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party, which drove the rival PUK from the city exactly one week ago.
Jolles said he had spoken to the four on Monday morning, adding they appeared to be in good health. "But we can only say more once we've had an opportunity to really speak to them."
